title: Chicken & potatoes
description: A simple chicken-and-potato meal-prep base. The portion guide below comes from my saved five-container batch; adjust your own meal to what you need.
imageAlt: Seasoned sliced chicken and potatoes on a plate in James's kitchen.
caption: Chicken and potatoes from my kitchen. The pictured plate is a different serving from the portion guide below.
ingredients: 1,000 g cooked chicken breast (200 g per container)
300 g baked potato slices (60 g per container)
Cooking spray, as needed
Salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika, to taste
steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. Cook until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C), checked with a food thermometer. Rest, then slice or dice.
Slice the potatoes evenly, lightly coat with cooking spray and season. Bake at 425°F until browned and tender, flipping once. The time will depend on slice thickness and your oven.
Weigh the chicken and potatoes after cooking. Divide 1,000 g cooked chicken and 300 g baked potatoes among five containers: 200 g chicken and 60 g potatoes in each.
Cool and refrigerate promptly in shallow containers. Follow the storage guidance below; freeze portions you won't eat within the refrigerated window.
note: The quantities above describe the finished food. Cooking changes the weight, so don't use 1,000 g of raw chicken as a substitute for 1,000 g cooked. This is my recorded portion split, not a nutrition target for everyone.
nutritionNote: Nutrition will vary with the chicken, cooking fat, seasonings and portions. No unverified macro totals are included here.

title: Smoky chipotle beef pasta
description: Beef, penne and kidney beans with mozzarella and chipotle in adobo. This five-portion recipe comes from my meal-prep notebook.
ingredients: 2 lb lean ground beef
270 g dry Barilla Protein+ penne
430 g kidney beans, drained and rinsed
220 g reduced-fat mozzarella
200 g Rao's pizza sauce
50 g chipotle peppers in adobo, chopped
Salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder, to taste
steps: Cook the penne according to its package instructions until just tender, then drain.
Cook the ground beef over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Check that it reaches 160°F (71°C) with a food thermometer. Drain excess fat if needed and season to taste.
Stir in the drained kidney beans, pizza sauce and chopped chipotle peppers. Simmer for 3–5 minutes.
Fold in the pasta and mozzarella until evenly combined and the cheese has melted.
Divide into five portions. Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers and use the storage guidance below.
note: These are the brands and amounts recorded in my notebook. Changing the beef, pasta or cheese changes the nutrition. Add the ingredients you actually use to your own food log if you track.
nutritionNote: Contains wheat and dairy in the listed pasta and cheese; check your exact labels for other allergens. Nutrition totals are being left out until the labels and finished yield are checked.

title: Cheesy jalapeño ranch chicken burritos
description: Chipotle chicken, cheesy jalapeño ranch sauce and a tortilla toasted in a skillet. Makes six burritos.
imageAlt: Cheesy jalapeño ranch sauce in a pan beside a burrito toasting in a skillet.
caption: The sauce and a burrito in the skillet.
ingredients: 8 oz Philadelphia 1/3 Less Fat Cream Cheese
7 oz Great Value Reduced Fat Fiesta Blend Shredded Cheese
1 packet Hidden Valley Ranch Dip Mix (1 oz)
1 can La Victoria Mild Diced Green Chiles (can size not specified)
1 can Great Value Hot Diced Jalapeño Peppers (can size not specified)
A small splash of water, if needed
2 lb Costco Chargrilled Chipotle Chicken (about 151 g per burrito)
6 Don Pancho Carb Control Tortillas
Up to 600 g of the prepared sauce (100 g per burrito, if the batch makes enough)
steps: Warm the cream cheese in a saucepan over low to medium-low heat, stirring until softened. Add the shredded cheese gradually and stir until melted.
Mix in the ranch dip mix, green chiles and diced jalapeños. Stir until combined and creamy; add a little water if the sauce needs thinning.
Heat the chargrilled chipotle chicken according to its package directions. Divide the 2 lb package into six portions, about 151 g each.
Weigh the finished sauce. If it makes at least 600 g, use 100 g per burrito. If it makes less, divide what you have evenly rather than assuming the full amount.
Place one tortilla flat, add one portion of chicken and sauce, fold in the sides and roll tightly. Repeat for all six burritos.

If you like, toast the burritos in a skillet until golden on both sides. Cool and wrap individually or place in airtight containers before refrigerating or freezing. Reheat following the guidance below.
note: The supplied recipe calls for 600 g of prepared sauce, split six ways. It does not give the can sizes or a measured sauce yield, so weigh the finished batch before portioning.
nutritionNote: The supplied nutrition estimates are not included because the can sizes, exact product labels and finished sauce yield have not been verified. Check your ingredient labels for allergens; the listed sauce contains dairy.
